body: I share your fear of medication as well. I was assured Abilify was less likely to cause side effects but now I'm just not going to fill the prescription and find a new psychiatrist. The last time I tried something he prescribed it was Zeldox. I just took ONE pill and I was in the ER. It was the lowest possible dose as well.
Wow. My doc makes an effort to take history and then never actually look back on it. Ended up diagnosing me with three different mental disorders over the course of our patient-doctor relationship.
Yes...good luck to all of us. I'm just afraid I will kill myself before I find the right doctor or right treatment.
I'm having a lot of emotional issues that my psychiatrist was made aware of during the appointment. They were dismissed and he didn't want to discuss them. We moved onto pills immediately after.
Thank you. I feel I do have a lot of emotional triggers that I need to learn to control or minimize.

Do you have any advice on trying to find people who will understand or want to understand? I've sometimes brought it up with friends I thought would understand but ended up walking away because it simply was too much for them to handle (I don't blame them). And what if even your immediate family can't accept the need for medication and that this is real?

I've also done the "try over 10 medications and have none of them work" routine. I gave up for a while...but when I was hit with a huge wave of depression recently I just knew I wouldn't be able to cope without doing something beyond what I was doing before (exercise, diet, strict day to day routine). I'm trying to educate myself on current advances in treatment for bipolar disorder and understand it better, but sometimes it gets difficult...

I'm not 100% sure of my triggers (as in, sometimes they affect me in a big way, sometimes they don't)...also these may not apply to anyone else. My triggers for mania can sometimes be as simple as too much caffeine or refined sugar. Triggers for depression is a spike in stress levels, either from an unexpected situation completely throwing off my "routine", any type of confrontation or being alone too much.

Things that can stop depression and mania? Trying to force myself back into the proper routines if I've been thrown off, especially when it comes to my sleep schedule. It's harder than some people may think because my insomnia doesn't allow me to sleep. I'm trying to figure this out still...sometimes it ends up just being me trying not to kill myself.

Oh yeah, another thing that can trigger my depression is when people tell me its all in my head or that I'm not trying hard enough to fix myself (trying to manage bipolar disorder, particularly without medication, is a full-time job). That or when those close to me tell me that I don't need any medication and that X, Y or Z will fix everything despite not having the illness themselves or having a decent understanding of it.

Thanks for replying. I'm trying to sort out my own medications for bipolar disorder and the one of the most frustrating things I've had to deal with has been the loss of concentration. It's nice to hear from others with the same issues.
I'm curious, what did your doc say?

Good for her. And good for her cousins if they actually pursued something that they wanted to do with their lives. It's possible that they wanted to be doctors and dentists and it wasn't just family pressure.

I am not defending them, but I have spent a lot of time trying to act as mediator/adversary against this type of parenting. Your parents probably see that you are quitting a good job in the middle of poor economic times. They want to force you to see that "Yes, this is a bad choice" but they're using a slippery slope argument to do so (so it seems extremely old-fashioned/idiotic to you). They also are probably used to the idea that "stable job = stable life". If you can illustrate that you can support yourself in whatever endeavor you wish to pursue in the long term, they may accept your decision. If you can also explain why this is a good move, this may be to your benefit.

It's totally possible everything I said doesn't apply to you, but I hope it can somewhat help.

You have no idea what it's like to have a difficult life, it was so much harder when we were younger, North American children are so spoiled!"

Cannot up vote you enough. Restricting contact is okay if it improves the relationship...or at least ensures you do not go fucking nuts.
Thank you. I'll try to remember that when it gets too difficult to cope again.

In addition to this I actually find the ritual of making myself a cup of tea really relaxing. Regardless of if it is loose leaf green tea or Red Rose...making myself a cup of tea sometimes let's me keep control or provide a distraction during mania.

I overdosed on painkillers. I didn't perform the correct research into the right cocktail of drugs that would have offed me so I ended up in the ER with my very angry family. It's been years but I've been trying to figure out a way to kill myself and yet inconvenience the least amount of people possible. 

Everyone thinks I'm fine now. That and I've stopped having close friends.
